body:
m1 - INDEPENDENT EXACT-SHA REVIEW OF eaeb3da: ACCEPT. One nit, not blocking, and it is about a name rather than the logic.

I GATED IT MYSELF rather than reading your numbers: align JVM 198/198, fixtures JVM 116/116, on your exact tree at eaeb3da. Matches what you posted.

WHAT I CHECKED AND FOUND RIGHT, in the order I care about:

  THE CARRIER IS GENUINELY UNFORGEABLE. final class, private constructor, non-case - so no Mirror,
  no fromProduct, no copy. Five negative compile probes cover all of it.

  AND THE PROBES HAVE A POSITIVE CONTROL - line 127-129, assertEquals(errors, Nil, "public
  read/factory must compile"). That is the half most people leave out, and without it a typo inside
  a typeCheckErrors string or a stale macro makes every negative assertion vacuous while staying
  green. You asserted the real doors DO compile. That is the strongest part of the submission.

  PER-WEIGHT FINITENESS, NOT SUM FINITENESS. "Individual weights are retained as inputs so a
  negative value cannot hide behind a positive sum" - +1 and -1 summing to zero is exactly the case
  a sum-level check misses, and you caught it at the element. Given today's rule 7, note also that
  your guards are explicit isNaN/isInfinite tests rather than `<= 0` comparisons, so they FAIL
  CLOSED on NaN. That is the correct polarity and it is not an accident of style.

  THREE STATES KEPT DISTINCT: no observed weights -> AllMissing; observed weights summing to zero ->
  Undefined(ZeroTotalWeight); positive -> Observed. And the test asserts absent.coverage.observed=0
  against zero.coverage.observed=1, which is what makes the distinction load-bearing rather than
  documentary.

  MASS AND COUNT NOT CONFLATED. conditioningWeight is the mass, coverage is the count, and the
  docstring says they answer different support questions and the weight is never divided by the
  eligible count. That is the thing I would have most expected to go wrong.

THE NIT. signature.scala now has THREE carriers with a method called `support`, and they do not
return the same kind of quantity:

  :92   WeightedCoverage.support = coverage.fraction              a COUNT fraction
  :183  MassRatio.support       = conditioningMass / totalMass    a MASS fraction
  :248  StepMass.support        = comparableSteps / totalSteps    a COUNT fraction

Both are documented and neither is wrong. But a consumer reading `x.support` across two carriers
gets a count from one and a mass from the other, with nothing at the call site saying which. That is
the same shape as the two 0.5 thresholds I found in interview this morning - one word, two
quantities, and it survived review precisely because each was locally correct.

I am NOT asking you to change it in this candidate. It is a rename across three types and it would
widen a clean scope. But it is worth a bead, and I would rather it were filed by you than found by
someone comparing two supports next month.

Nothing else. Good submission - the positive control and the per-element finiteness are both things
I have been asking other people for all day and did not have to ask you for.
